title: Crux Logistics POC kickoff & timeline
summary: Kickoff POC scoping for Crux Logistics. Agreed on success criteria (latency/SLA and accuracy), workload sizing for peak batch jobs and steady-state RPS, benchmark plan, and a 4-week timeline with milestones: kickoff, access+env setup, mid-point review, exec readout. Action items assigned for Redwood to share SOW, benchmark scripts, and for Crux to provide sample traffic and VPC details.
next_steps: Jordan to send POC SOW and pricing (by 2026-04-16)
Priya to share benchmark scripts and KB for access (by 2026-04-20)
Crux to provide sanitized sample traffic and data schema (by 2026-04-19)
action_items: Priya - provide benchmark script + runbook - due 2026-04-20
Jordan - send SOW + pricing + success criteria doc - due 2026-04-16
Martin - share sample traffic (sanitized) and target KPIs - due 2026-04-19
Liam - provide VPC peering details and admin contact for networking - due 2026-04-18
transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2026-04-15 | Start: 14:00 UTC | Duration: 48 mins
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Natarajan (Redwood SE), Martin Reyes (Crux - Head of ML), Sasha Kim (Crux - CTO), Liam Patel (Crux - Infra)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE on this account, and with me is Priya, our solutions engineer. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Martin: Martin here, hello.
[00:08] Sasha: Sasha on the call.
[00:10] Liam: Liam, infra.
[00:12] Priya: Great, thanks. We're here to scope the POC timeline and milestones, make sure success criteria are clear, and nail down what we'll benchmark.
[00:22] Jordan: Quick agenda: success criteria, workload sizing, benchmark plan, access and security, timeline and milestones, next steps. Anything to add?
[00:27] Sasha: Nope that's good. Also want to touch on any compliance pre-reqs - SOC 2 stuff - briefly.
[00:31] Jordan: Absolutely, we'll add that.

[02:00] Priya: To start success criteria, what does Crux want to prove in this POC? Is it latency at scale, cost per 1k tokens, quality/regression versus your current models?
[02:12] Martin: Primary is inference latency and stable throughput for our routing engine. We need 95th percentile under 350ms for single-turn inference on typical payloads. Also accuracy - we measure retrieval+ranker F1 and endpoint correctness, but latency is primary.
[02:28] Priya: Okay 95p < 350ms sounds reasonable as a POC target. Are you measuring tokens per request? Typical prompt sizes?
[02:35] Martin: Typical prompts are around 120 tokens, sometimes up to 400 for rare cases. Average is 120. Peak traffic for live routing is ~80 RPS with bursts to 200 for 30s. But most traffic is batch scoring at night - roughly 1M requests over a 2 hour window.
[02:54] Jordan: Helpful. So we have two workload shapes: steady low-latency RPS and high-throughput batch window. We'll size both in the benchmark.

[04:00] Priya: For benchmarks we'll run two profiles: 1) interactive latency profile at steady-state 80 RPS with burst testing to 200 RPS, measuring p50/p95/p99 and token cost; 2) batch throughput profile for the nighttime 1M requests over 2 hours to measure sustained throughput and cost per 1K tokens. We'll use sample traffic you provide and a sanitized dataset.
[04:22] Martin: Good. Also want to validate Redwood Dedicated vs Hosted with autoscale - what's realistic? We care about predictable latency so Dedicated is interesting.
[04:32] Priya: We can test both. For Dedicated we'll provision reserved GPU pool to get predictable latency; for Hosted we'll show fallback policies and region routing. Note: Dedicated numbers depend on quantization and kernel choices; we'll recommend specific quantization profiles after initial runs.

[06:00] Sasha: On security: we need SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, and KMS integration. Also data residency - all inference logs must stay in EU.
[06:12] Jordan: Understood. For POC we can do VPC peering to a Redwood Private control plane or set up private endpoints; for logs we can configure retention and region. We'll share the security checklist.

[08:00] Liam: Quick question on access: we manage infra so will need to set up VPC peering and IAM roles. What do you need from us?
[08:08] Priya: We'll need account IDs, CIDR ranges for peering, and an admin contact. If you use KMS, we'll need policy for key usage or we can demo with temporary keys. Also SSH for initial debug in Dedicated if required.
[08:20] Liam: Got it, I can provide peering info.

[10:00] Jordan: Timeline proposal: Week 0 (kickoff) Apr 22 - environment set up and creds exchanged. Week 1 - access and baseline benchmarks. Week 2 - mid-point review and tuning (quantization, batching profiles). Week 3 - final benchmarks and cost analysis. Week 4 - exec readout and decision. That's a 4-week POC. Thoughts?
[10:22] Martin: That works. Can we shift exec readout to May 13? That aligns with our SLT calendar.
[10:28] Jordan: We can do May 13. So kickoff Apr 22, mid-point May 6, exec May 13.

[12:00] Priya: On deliverables: Redwood will provide a SOW + success criteria doc, benchmark scripts, a runbook for access, and a short onboarding checklist for networking. Crux provides sample traffic, expected KPIs, and a point of contact for infra.
[12:16] Martin: We'll provide a sanitized sample of traffic schemas and labels. Also we'll include our current latency baseline so you can compare.

[14:00] Jordan: Pricing and reserved capacity options - I'll send the initial SOW with two options: hosted usage-based and Dedicated with 3-month reserved capacity. For the POC we typically cover trial Dedicated hours but list estimated committed costs so execs understand next steps.
[14:22] Sasha: Good. We need the cost-per-1k tokens and a projected monthly cost at 80 RPS and at peak batch runs.
[14:30] Priya: We'll produce a cost model spreadsheet showing both throughput and expected monthly spend across quantization profiles.

[16:00] Martin: A few technical nitpicks: our model chain uses heavy KV cache hits from retrieval; how do you manage KV cache across requests? Does Redwood expose cache affinity?
[16:12] Priya: We support KV cache and prefix caching; for multi-tenant Hosted we do opaque caching, but for Dedicated we can configure local cache affinity and persistent KV layers. There was a minor transcription issue in previous calls where KV cache became "K V cash" in notes, just flagging that.
[16:32] Martin: Ha, yes saw that.

[18:00] Liam: Network egress: if we do Private deployment, what bandwidth ceilings do we need? Our batch window is intense.
[18:08] Priya: We'll size GPU pools to avoid egress bottlenecks; typical batch window for 1M requests over 2 hours at 120 tokens avg is X - we'll run numbers in the benchmark plan and include expected egress. (Note: here the transcript sometimes substitutes numbers; final spreadsheet will include exact math.)

[20:00] Jordan: Action items recap: Jordan send SOW and pricing, Priya share benchmark scripts, Crux provide sample traffic and peering info, Liam provide admin contact. Mid-point review scheduled for May 6. Exec readout May 13. Any blockers?
[20:18] Martin: None immediate. We'll aim to get artifacts by Apr 19 so you can prep before kickoff.
[20:24] Sasha: Also, we need to validate compliance docs - can you share SOC 2 and ISO artifacts?
[20:30] Jordan: Yes, I'll attach our compliance pack.

[22:00] Priya: Technical note for the bench: we'll run p95 and p99 with 1% tail runs and include token-cost metric. For batch we'll measure sustained tokens per second and cost per 1k tokens. We'll also test quantized model variants (int8 vs int4) to show cost/latency tradeoffs.
[22:25] Martin: We'll want to see quality delta when you quantize (QA numbers). If quality drops too much we may prefer Dedicated FP16.

[24:00] Jordan: Anything else on roadmap or milestones?
[24:06] Liam: Make sure the onboarding runbook mentions iptables rules and the internal NAT settings for our VPC, we've run into that before.
[24:12] Priya: Noted, we'll add a troubleshooting section.

[30:00] Jordan: Quick recap of milestones: Kickoff & access (Apr 22), baseline and Hosted/Dedicated baseline benchmarks (Apr 22-29), mid-point tuning and derived configs (May 6), final benchmarking and cost analysis (May 7-11), exec readout (May 13).
[30:24] Martin: That aligns.

[36:00] Sasha: For the exec readout we'll need a 20-minute slide deck covering: findings, cost model, recommended deployment (Hosted vs Dedicated), risk and next steps. Can Redwood prepare a deck template?
[36:12] Jordan: Yes, we'll prepare a recommended deck and slide template.

[40:00] Priya: Clarifying success criteria pack: we'll capture latency targets, quality thresholds (F1 >= current baseline - 1%), and cost targets (cost per 1k tokens or monthly run cost under x). We'll put those in the SOW.
[40:20] Martin: Agree. Also add rollback criteria - if p95 increases above 400ms in production we want an automatic failover plan.
[40:28] Priya: Noted, we'll include fallback policy options (model variant fallback, regional fallback).

[44:00] Jordan: Ok last checks - anything blocking to start the access work?
[44:06] Liam: I'll gather peering and IAM details this week and send to Jordan.
[44:10] Martin: I'll sanitize sample data and send.
[44:12] Sasha: We'll review the SOW with the CFO once you send it.

[47:00] Jordan: Great, thanks everyone. I'll send the notes and SOW tomorrow. Priya will follow up with the bench scripts. Talk soon.
[47:12] Martin: Thanks all.
[47:15] End of transcript.
